saints.name: St. Ephrem the Syrian
saints.title: Deacon and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The “Harp of the Holy Spirit,” whose hymns taught the faith and adorned the worship of the Syriac Church…
biography: Born at Nisibis in Roman Mesopotamia about 306, Ephrem was baptized young and served his church as deacon and teacher under Bishop Jacob. He lived through three Persian sieges of his city, and when the Emperor Jovian ceded Nisibis to Persia in 363 he went into exile with its Christian people, settling at Edessa.

There he taught in the famous school and poured out hymns, verse homilies, and commentaries in Syriac, defending the Nicene faith against Arians, Marcionites, Manichees, and the followers of Bardaisan. His teaching hymns were sung by choirs of women in the churches; more than four hundred survive, besides his commentary on the Diatessaron.

For the sweetness of that song he was called the Harp of the Spirit, and the Syriac Church reveres him as its greatest father. In 370 he visited Basil at Caesarea. Worn out by ministry to the famine-stricken and sick of Edessa, he died there in 373; Benedict XV declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1920.
saints.knownFor: His hymns and the title “Harp of the Holy Spirit.”

canonization.canonized: Venerated from antiquity; declared a Doctor of the Church in 1920
